title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a continuation of La Longue Marche, written after the section of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' numbered 549 and before §49 (p. 550). M_{0,3}^~ is an extension of a Galois-type group Γ_{0,3}^~ ⊃ Γ_Q by the profinite loop/mapping-class group S_{0,3}^{+∧}. Θ_ρ^π and Θ_σ^π are the 'lines', meaning base-point or path data attached to the two elliptic generators ρ and σ (orders 2 and 3). These generators come from the elliptic fixed points of the S_3-action on M_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}:
- the orbit (1/2, 2, −1), whose Legendre curve has j = 1728 and CM by Z[i];
- the orbit (−j, −j̄), with j a primitive cube root of unity, whose curve has j-invariant 0 and CM by Z[ζ_3].

On the previous page, relations (35) and (36) are interpreted as the Γ_Q-action on Tate modules of these CM elliptic curves. A sign ambiguity remains there, coming from lifting a point of M_{1,1}[2]' = M_{0,3} to M_{1,1}[2], i.e. choosing an elliptic curve with level-2 (Legendre) rigidification, which amounts to a quadratic twist.

This page states the following.
- One ambiguity in the choice of 'lines' (the one for Θ_{ρ_3}^π, apparently) disappears once one passes to the genus-one extension T_{1,1}^~ and to the 'Jenseits' of M_{0,3}^~.
- The ambiguity for Θ_ρ^π and Θ_σ^π nevertheless persists. The reason is that the half-lines (tangential base points, or 'particules') Ψ_{1/2}^π and Ψ_{−j}^π at the elliptic points are half-lines only for M_{0,3}^~, not for T_{1,1}^~.
- The coverings over T_{1,1} needed to lift these half-lines correspond exactly to choosing elliptic curves with Legendre rigidification over λ = 1/2 and λ = −j.
- Conclusion: computations done purely in terms of the action of the profinite loop groups π_{0,3}^ on C̃_{0,3}^{+∧} ('if one had looked for them!') yield relations that match closely with crucial arithmetic-geometric facts. These facts are the Galois representations on Tate modules of the CM curves, i.e. CM/Hecke characters, up to a twist.

The problem served is understanding the arithmetic meaning of the 2- and 3-cycle ('elliptic') relations satisfied by the Galois/GT action on π_{0,3}^, and the role of genus-one lifting in removing base-point ambiguities.
errors: No mathematical error detectable; the claims are qualitative. The residual sign/twist ambiguity is correctly identified as the choice of lift from M_{1,1}[2]' to M_{1,1}[2] (quadratic twist).
The exact meaning of 'lignes' and which ambiguity is removed (Θ_{ρ_3}?) cannot be fully determined from this page alone.

ideas.what: Elliptic fixed points 1/2 and −j of the S_3-action on P^1−{0,1,∞} correspond to the CM elliptic curves with j = 1728 and j = 0 (Legendre curves). The Galois action on paths or tangential base points there should reproduce the Galois action on their Tate modules (CM characters).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on paths to CM / elliptic points; Jacobi-sum and CM-character interpretation of Galois action on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) evaluated at special points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Anderson (hyperadelic gamma function), Ihara–Kaneko–Yukinari (universal power series for Jacobi sums, 1987), Nakamura (explicit formulae, Eisenstein-type representations, genus-one work)

ideas.what: Base-point ambiguities at elliptic points are partly but not fully resolved by lifting to the genus-one tower T_{1,1}. The remaining indeterminacy is exactly the choice of a Legendre-rigidified elliptic curve (level-2 lift).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the GT/Galois action between M_{0,4} (≈ M_{1,1}[2]) and M_{1,1}; tangential base points on the modular curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Nakamura–Schneps (GT acting on genus-one Teichmüller tower, 2000); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the role of M_{1,1} but not this specific analysis

ideas.what: Purely combinatorial or group-theoretic computations in the profinite loop group 'recover' arithmetic relations: the relations (35) and (36) match Galois representations on CM Tate modules.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic content of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara for the relations; arithmetic interpretation partly by Ihara, Anderson, Nakamura

missed.quote: des revêtements sur T_{1,1} … servant très précisément à choisir justement des courbes elliptiques à signification de Legendre en dessus des pts 1/2, −J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give a conceptual explanation of the 2- and 3-cycle relations of GT via CM theory. It also points to explicit tests of GT versus Gal(Q̄/Q) at elliptic points of the genus-one tower.

missed.claim: On the previous page Grothendieck says he did not try to prove the coincidence up to sign. Here he states that the loop-group computations would 'redonner' the arithmetic relations, without carrying this out.
missed.quote: (si on les avait cherchés!) redonnent des résultats qui collent de très près à des relations arithmético-géométriques particulièrement cruciales
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an explicit verification programme. Compute the GT/Galois action on the half-lines at 1/2 and −j and compare it with the CM characters. It is partially addressed but not obviously completed in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: An interesting unpublished heuristic tying the GT elliptic relations and genus-one lifting to CM Tate modules. However, closely related themes (Anderson, Ihara's Jacobi sums, Nakamura's genus-one work) are developed in the literature, and the page is qualitative.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out word before Ψ_{1/2}^π, Ψ_{−J}^π is illegible; there is a stray ')' after Ψ_{−J}^π, suggesting an earlier opening parenthesis.
'par choix pour autres' is doubtful; it is perhaps 'pour l'instant' or similar.
'redonnent' may be 'redonneraient' or 'redonnent' (the image reads 'ae donnent').
Line 'des groupes à lacets π_{0,3}^ dans C̃_{0,3}^{+∧}': the 'dans' is written over a small arrow, so it may instead be '→'.
'des revêtements sur T_{1,1}' is an insertion written above the line.
